title: At the fruit shop
summary: A customer buys apples and asks about prices.

sentences.en: Hello, how much are the apples?
These apples are five yuan each.
Five yuan? That's too expensive! What about those?
Those are cheap, two yuan each.
Very tasty! Look, they're big too.

sentences.zh: 六个十二块。你还要什么？
sentences.en: Six is twelve yuan. Anything else?

questions.prompt: Why doesn't she buy the first apples?
why: Size isn't her complaint about the first apples.
She doesn't say they aren't tasty.

questions.prompt: How many apples does she buy?
why: Five yuan was the price of the first apples.
Two yuan is the price of each apple she buys.
Right: 六个十二块 — six apples at two yuan each.
That would be six of the five-yuan apples.
Six is the number of apples, not the price.
